title: Nilpotence of an element in a residue fibre is detected by the characteristic polynomial

standard_prerequisites.name: Cayley-Hamilton for the multiplication map
standard_prerequisites.use: Ties nilpotence of the multiplication map to the vanishing of the characteristic polynomial.

standard_prerequisites.name: Behaviour of the characteristic polynomial under base change to a residue field
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the characteristic polynomial of the fibre with the reduction of the original one.

core_obligations: Show the characteristic polynomial of the multiplication map after base change to the residue field is the reduction of the given one, so that its coefficients are the images of the r_i (proof lines 5786-5808).
Conclude: the element acts nilpotently exactly when that fibre polynomial equals T^n by Cayley-Hamilton, which happens exactly when all the r_i lie in the prime (proof lines 5808-5811).
proof_roadmap: Compare the characteristic polynomial with its fibre version (proof lines 5785-5808).
Read nilpotence off the vanishing of the coefficients (proof lines 5808-5812).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map whose target is finite free of rank n as a module, an element acts nilpotently on the fibre at a prime exactly when that prime contains the first n coefficients of the characteristic polynomial (statement lines 5771-5783). The proof does not use determinants of the action on generators: it compares the fibre characteristic polynomial with the reduction of the given one, applies Cayley-Hamilton on both sides, and reads the condition off the coefficients (proof lines 5785-5812). Reducing modulo the prime so that the two polynomials agree is the step that carries the argument. H2.
